findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, meaning objects stored in it are not encrypted at rest by default, increasing risk of data exposure if underlying storage or backups are compromised.

findings.issue_category: no bucket ACL / public access controls
findings.description: No ACL is defined and there is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource associated, so the bucket could default to being more permissive than intended and is not explicitly protected against public access.
This bucket stores sensitive ledger export data but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving financial data unencrypted at rest.

There is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource to explicitly block public ACLs/policies on this sensitive bucket, relying only on the default 'private' ACL which can be overridden by bucket policy or ACL changes.
The bucket has versioning and logging configured but lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block, so model artifacts are stored unencrypted.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so operational runbooks (which may contain sensitive operational details) are stored unencrypted.

The ACL value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid S3 canned ACL; if Terraform coerces or AWS defaults this to something like 'log-delivery-write' or fails open, it could grant broader write/read access than intended to the audit trail bucket, which holds sensitive audit logs and encryption is otherwise the last line of defense.

This object is uploaded to reports_archive, which has no server-side encryption configured, meaning the vendor roster file (potentially containing sensitive vendor/PII data) is stored unencrypted and without any per-object encryption override (e.g., kms_key_id) specified.

force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be destroyed without recovery, which combined with lack of versioning increases risk of irreversible data loss that could be triggered by an attacker with delete permissions.
